title: Cross-engine vector search — 4 engines, one harness
subtitle: MyVector · vsql_vector · pgvector · MariaDB — fashion-mnist-784, published ground truth
description: A cross-engine comparison run through a neutral third-party harness — VillageSQL's vector-dev-bench (the MyVector profile is upstream PR #14). Same real dataset (fashion-mnist-784-euclidean, 60k × 784, L2) and published exact ground truth drive all three engines; this answers "how does MyVector's HNSW compare to VillageSQL's own vsql_vector, pgvector, and MariaDB's native vector indexes on the same workload and harness?" (The other pages compare MyVector across MySQL versions.)
caveats: Harness: VillageSQL vector-dev-bench recall_bench.py — one PyMySQL/psql path, numpy ground truth. The MyVector engine profile is upstream PR #14. It reports build time + a recall@10/QPS ef_search sweep; insert and exact-KNN columns aren't produced by this harness, so they show “—”.
Dataset & recall: fashion-mnist-784-euclidean (60k train × 784-d, 10k test, L2) with recall@10 scored against the dataset's published exact neighbors (ann-benchmarks methodology).
Index params: HNSW M=16, ef_construction=200 for MyVector and pgvector. MariaDB's MHNSW fixes ef_construction at 10 internally (not tunable) — documented, not matched.

Cache fairness: each engine's graph sized to stay in memory above the ~188 MB index — MyVector loads its HNSW into its own memory (InnoDB pool 2 GB for the build scan); MariaDB mhnsw_max_cache_size=1 GiB; pgvector shared_buffers=2 GB.
Headline cards are the warm ef_search=200 sweep point, so all three engines are compared at one operating point.
Hardware: all three on the same A2 host (8 vCPU / 24 GB), each container pinned to 4 vCPU / 16 GB.
